answers.is_the_bucket_about_the_studies_or_the_i: the instrument: the members exist under another name or in a constant for 63 of 180 studies, and 107 of them never parse source text at all, so the BOM question cannot bite them whether or not their corpus is readable

unreadable_rows.reading: the rows this scan cannot parse are themselves BOM-prefixed sources, so three members of E502's own bucket are unreadable for exactly the reason E502 was measuring

method_limits: the population is E502's corpus_exposed=false rows (183 of 201) carried as a set of source paths; the gate re-derives every count from the rows, but cannot re-decide which studies E502 could price
surfaces are read statically from the module's own AST -- nothing is imported, executed or fetched, so a callable that would fail at runtime still counts as a surface and no constant is valued

name matching is a token test (corpus/sources/members/universe/panel/files/...), with a negative token list (skip/ignore/exclude/...) so an exclusion list is not published as a member list; a plausible-looking name that fails the test is published as names_nothing, never guessed
only module-level statements are read: a surface built inside a function body or assigned in a branch is invisible to this scan
the adapter string is a suggestion of the cheapest read, not a claim that the value it returns equals the study's corpus -- that would need execution
reader_class is E502's field carried verbatim; the cross table prices the question 'does this study even parse source text' but cannot re-decide the class
title: Of the studies E502 could not price for want of a zero-argument corpus(), what does each module actually expose, and could a one-line adapter read it?
